title: A polyphasic method for the characterization of epiphytic diatoms growing on Gelidium corneum
author: Borrego-Ramos, Viso, et al.
materials: The PCR2 reaction was carried out in a final volume of 25 µL, containing 2.5 µL of DNA from the received PCR products, 1 µM of primers with dual indices, 6.5 µL of Supreme NZYTaq 2x Green Master Mix (NZYTech), and ultrapure water up to 25 µL. The reaction mixture was incubated as follows: initial denaturation at 95 °C for 5 min, followed by 5 cycles of 95 °C for 30 s, 60 °C for 45 s, 72 °C for 45 s, and a final extension at 72 °C for 7 min. A negative control (BPCR) containing no DNA was included in each PCR round to check for contamination during library preparation. Libraries were run on a 2% agarose gel stained with GreenSafe (NZYTech), and images were captured under UV light to verify library size. Libraries were purified using Mag-Bind® RXNPure Plus magnetic beads (Omega Biotek), following the manufacturer's instructions. Subsequently, libraries were pooled in equimolar amounts based on quantification data provided by the Qubit™ dsDNA HS assay (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Pooling was sequenced on a fraction of a MiSeq PE300 run (Illumina).

steps.title: Collect and preserve specimens
steps.instruction: Scuba‑dive to depths of 5 m and 15 m at the two sites, cut healthy Gelidium corneum specimens from the base, place each in a 1 L container, decant seawater at surface and add 70 % ethanol until fully submerged, then store containers in cool boxes for transport.

steps.title: Store samples before processing
steps.instruction: Upon arrival at the laboratory, keep the ethanol‑preserved specimens at 4 °C in darkness until further processing.

steps.title: Prepare samples for morphology
steps.instruction: For each specimen, take 100–400 mL of material, let it settle for 24 h, carefully remove the supernatant, pipette 10 mL of the remaining sediment into tubes, centrifuge at 5000 rpm for 5 min, discard supernatant, add 5 mL H₂O₂ to the pellet, homogenise, transfer to test tubes and oxidise with 5 mL H₂O₂ for 12 h in a water or sand bath; after a further 12 h settlement add a few drops of HCl to dissolve carbonates, wash twice with distilled water, finally dilute the frustules in 5 mL distilled water (or 1:10 if salty), place 1 mL on a coverslip and fix with Naphrax® on a hot plate.

steps.title: Microscopy and valve counting
steps.instruction: Mount the coverslips on a bright‑field Olympus BX60 microscope equipped with DIC, UPlanApo VC 100 objective (1000×) and a 9 MP Optika camera; photograph frustules at 1000× and count at least 400 valves per sample.

steps.title: Prepare samples for DNA work
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at least 200 mL of each sample at 4000 rpm for 5 min at 4 °C, discard the supernatant and retain the pellet for DNA extraction.

steps.title: Extract DNA
steps.instruction: Use the PowerSoil DNA Isolation® kit (Mo Bio) following the manufacturer’s protocol to extract DNA from each pellet.

steps.title: First‑round rbcL PCR
steps.instruction: Set up three PCR replicates per DNA sample with 1 µL DNA in a 25 µL reaction containing 0.5 µL Phire® Hot Start II DNA Polymerase, 5 µL 5× Buffer, 2 µL dNTP mix (2 mM each), 0.25 µM of each primer (equimolar mix of forward Diat_rbcL_708F_1, _F_2, _F_3 and reverse Diat_rbcL_R3_1, _R3_2 with Illumina P5/P7 adapters), and 14.5 µL nuclease‑free water; thermocycle: 94 °C 4 min; 40 cycles of 94 °C 30 s, 55 °C 30 s, 68 °C 30 s; final extension 68 °C 10 min.

steps.title: Check PCR products by gel
steps.instruction: Run 1.5 % agarose gels stained with ethidium bromide, visualize bands under UV light to confirm rbcL amplification.

steps.title: Second‑round indexing PCR (PCR2)
steps.instruction: Prepare a 25 µL reaction with 2.5 µL of the first‑PCR product, 1 µM dual‑index primers, 6.5 µL Supreme NZYTaq 2× Green Master Mix, and water to volume; thermocycle: 95 °C 5 min; 5 cycles of 95 °C 30 s, 60 °C 45 s, 72 °C 45 s; final extension 72 °C 7 min. Include a negative control (BPCR) with no DNA.

steps.title: Validate indexed libraries
steps.instruction: Run the PCR2 products on 2 % agarose gels stained with GreenSafe, capture images under UV to verify library size.

steps.title: Purify and pool libraries
steps.instruction: Purify libraries using Mag‑Bind® RXNPure Plus magnetic beads per the manufacturer’s instructions, quantify each with Qubit™ dsDNA HS assay, then pool them in equimolar amounts.

steps.title: Sequence libraries
steps.instruction: Submit the pooled library for Illumina MiSeq PE300 sequencing (partial run).

steps.title: Bioinformatic processing
steps.instruction: Process raw reads with the DADA2 pipeline in R using the diat.barcode package: filter, remove chimeras, generate ASVs, and assign taxonomy against the Diat.barcode v7 reference database.

description: This method was tested on samples collected from two locations along the northern coast of Spain, specifically within the Cantabria region: near San Vicente de la Barquera and Noja (43° 22′ 59″ N, 4° 24′ 01″ W and 43° 28′ 53″ N, 3° 31′ 07″ W, respectively), during June 2022 (Fig. 1). The Cantabrian coast features a temperate-humid climate influenced by Atlantic winds predominantly coming from the W-NW, although under anticyclonic conditions NE winds dominate [36]. Mean seawater temperature along this coastline typically range from approximately 12 °C in winter to 20 °C in summer, reflecting the moderating effect of the oceanic currents [37].Fig. 1Map of the sampling sites of the study on the north coast of Spain: San Vicente de la Barquera and Noja.Fig 1 Depths of 5 and 15 m were chosen at both locations (San Vicente de la Barquera and Noja) for the specimen collection, corresponding to a typical habitat range of this species. Thus, these conditions were selected to ensure variation in light conditions. Healthy and robustly developed specimens of G. corneum were collected through scuba diving, cutting them from the base to ensure their future recovery. Then specimens were carefully introduced into containers of 1 L of capacity. Upon reaching the surface, seawater was decanted from the containers, and 70% alcohol was added until the samples were fully submerged. Subsequently, the containers were stored inside cool boxes and transported to the laboratory. Upon arrival samples were maintained at 4 °C in darkness until processing. Not applicable.
